name: Browse bounties and inspect the acceptance contract
description: Verifies visitors can inspect a bounty's acceptance criteria before attempting work.
steps: Open the app
Choose Explore bounties
Open a bounty card and inspect its acceptance criteria
expected: The board shows the agreed checks on the bounty, so contributors can understand what the owner will review before submitting.

name: Create a bounty with validated acceptance criteria
description: Verifies bounty creation permits one clear criterion for a narrow task, supports multiple criteria when needed, and retains a unique contract of 1–10 checks.
steps: Sign in
Choose Post a bounty
Enter a valid title, description, category and reward
Enter one clear acceptance criterion, or add more checks if the scope needs them
Publish and refresh the board
expected: The bounty is published and its acceptance criteria remain visible. A bounty with one valid criterion is published; empty, too-short, duplicated, and over-limit criteria are rejected.

name: Submit work against a snapshot of agreed criteria
description: Verifies submitted work is linked to the exact acceptance criteria agreed when the submission was made.
steps: Sign in as a contributor who does not own an open community bounty
Open a live bounty and read the acceptance criteria
Submit a written explanation and optionally add an evidence link
Open My contributions and refresh
If the existing-work indexing notice appears, use Continue until indexing is complete.
expected: The submission is pending review and retains the bounty's acceptance-criteria snapshot. Private per-user work views show the signed-in user's submissions and received reviews; existing records remain stored while bounded migration progresses.

name: Request changes, revise, and accept only the compliant version
description: Verifies the changes-requested cycle can produce a new submission version without losing prior review evidence or awarding XP twice.
steps: Owner requests changes and records which criteria are not yet met plus a written rationale
Original contributor opens My contributions and selects Revise & resubmit
Contributor updates the explanation or evidence and resubmits
Owner reviews the pending new version, sees the prior review event, checks every criterion, writes a rationale, and accepts
Refresh both views
expected: Version 2 returns to pending, revision 1 and the earlier review stay in history, a second independent submission is blocked while changes are requested, final acceptance records the passing checklist, and the contributor gains exactly 50 XP once.

name: Reject unauthorized and incomplete acceptance transitions
description: Verifies invalid acceptance data and unauthorized, duplicate, or out-of-order resubmissions are blocked by the backend.
steps: Publish a bounty with one valid criterion, then attempt empty, too-short, duplicated, and more-than-ten criterion lists
Attempt to accept work with a criterion still marked false or a rationale shorter than 15 characters
As someone other than the submitter, attempt to resubmit a changes-requested contribution
Try to create a second submission for a bounty where the existing submission has changes requested
Try to resubmit a contribution that is not in changes-requested status
expected: One clear criterion is allowed; empty, too-short, duplicated, or more-than-ten criteria are rejected. Review and ownership guards remain enforced, and invalid requests award no XP.

name: Review account roles and GitHub connection prerequisites
description: Verifies account settings explain the account, role boundaries and GitHub setup without claiming a connection before credentials are configured.
steps: Sign in with the existing ContribQuest account
Open Account & integrations
Inspect the account ID and current role
Inspect the GitHub configuration status and exact callback URL
Confirm repository installation is separate from identity linking and owner access requires server-side allowlisting
expected: The existing account remains canonical; roles come from server state, missing GitHub secrets appear as not configured, the callback URL is displayed exactly, and the interface never claims GitHub is linked or allows self-promotion to platform owner.
